A1.justification: Both PDFs describe SAGE and provide readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A.1–A.5. Relocated and renumbered material can be matched reliably.

before.justification: v2 reports original SAGE benchmark results, component ablations, runtime and convergence studies, sensitivity analyses, and qualitative evaluations.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experimental results in the main text and appendices.

M1.justification: The frozen DINOv2/DPN backbone, SoftP residual weighting, InteractHead, online geo-visual graph construction, and greedy weighted sampling remain unchanged. Sections 3.1–3.4 retain the same procedures.

E1.justification: Both versions use MSLS and GSV-Cities for training and the same eight main evaluation benchmarks. SF-small and the qualitative challenge scenarios were already included in v2's appendix.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the main benchmark tables, graph and convergence comparisons, SF-small comparison, and extended Table 13. Newly cited works such as SelaVPR++ are not added as evaluated baselines.

E3.justification: Training duration, input resolutions, backbone sizes, checkpoint selection, evaluation thresholds, descriptor dimensions, and graph settings remain unchanged. The InteractHead configurations in v2 Table 6 are retained in v3 Table 8.

E4.justification: The component and InteractHead ablations, online/offline comparison, convergence study, threshold sensitivity, clustering analyses, heatmaps, and failure examples are retained. The failure analysis moves from the main text to Appendix A.2.

E5.justification: Both versions report point estimates without repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, or significance tests. No statistical reporting procedure is added or revised.

E6.justification: Matched main-text and appendix result entries are unchanged, including 98.9% SPED R@1, 94.5% MSLS-val R@1, and 89.3% SF-small R@1. The plots, retrieval examples, and heatmap images retain the same results.

T1.justification: Equations 1–8, the SoftP variance reasoning and assumptions, graph and sampling definitions, and AID definition remain unchanged. No mathematical result or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central contributions and claims of dynamic geo-visual mining, parameter efficiency, and state-of-the-art performance across eight benchmarks remain. Adding 'Efficient' to the title and rewriting the conclusion emphasize existing claims.

C2.justification: v3 explains the existing InteractHead ablation through the SPED/Pitts30k tradeoff and a capacity/generalization rationale. Appendix A.5 expands prospective extensions to CLIP, multiple-view 3D representations, textual metadata, and topological cues; the substantive occlusion, scaling, and GPS limitations remain.

D1.justification: The abstract changes a promise to release code and models upon acceptance into a statement of availability at a specific SAGE repository. This adds concrete access information; repository functionality cannot be verified from the supplied PDFs. Implementation settings remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The bibliography adds works including NPR, SelaVPR++, and Deep Homography Estimation, while removing works including Bench2Drive and Segment Anything. The introduction modestly revises the motivation around joint geographic/visual sampling, while retaining the central positioning relative to EMVP and static mining.

P1.justification: v3 makes localized introduction, conclusion, and future-work rewrites, shortens the abstract, revises the title and affiliation/header text, and adds acknowledgments. Most method explanations and the document's section structure remain intact.

P2.justification: Tables 6–8 are reordered, and the failure figure moves from v2 Figure 6 to v3 Figure 9 in the appendix. Appendix figures and tables are resized or repositioned, with limited caption and formatting changes; their scientific content is retained.

improvement.justification: v3 provides a concrete code/model access pointer and explains the existing InteractHead configuration tradeoff more clearly, modestly improving reproducibility documentation and interpretation. Failure cases become less prominent after moving to the appendix, but remain available alongside the limitations. The unchanged experiments and mathematics support only a limited overall improvement.
